text:
Blackwood Bay was usually a symphony of low static and distant gulls. Tonight, though, the air felt different. David Vance leaned against the cold iron railing of the old pier, his breath pluming in the damp twilight. The usual drone of the town, the almost comforting static that bled from every ancient radio receiver in the forgotten corners of Blackwood Bay, had quieted. Not silenced, not entirely, but *muted*. Replaced by a strange, almost conscious hush that felt less like peace and more like a held breath.

He checked his recorder, the little red light blinking steadily, capturing the unsettling quiet. It wasn't the kind of stillness that precedes a storm, but a deeper, more deliberate kind. Beneath his worn boots, the pier seemed to thrum with a faint, almost imperceptible vibration, a low frequency that resonated more in his teeth than his ears. Too subtle for a truck, too steady for a boat. It was a pressure, an unseen hand pressing down, humming against the very foundations of the world. A tremor in the deeper currents, not of water, but of something far more ancient and unsettling.

This was Blackwood. The town had its own pulse, its own strange rhythms. But tonight, it felt like something vast and unseen had been on the verge of revealing itself, only to draw back at the last moment, leaving behind this peculiar silence and the ghost of a distant shockwave. Another piece of the puzzle, a whisper from the periphery of the known world, tightening the knot of the unanswered questions that had drawn David Vance into this darkening bay.
